My statement on becoming the Ranking Member of the Senate HELP Committee for the 120th Congress:

"Over the past two years, as Chairman of the Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee, I delivered the unprecedented oversight I promised. I challenged entrenched bureaucracies, forced federal officials to answer for their actions, and pulled back the curtain on what Washington tried to keep hidden. That included bringing Anthony Fauci before my committee under oath, bringing forward an Intelligence Community whistleblower who exposed what the government knew, and making thousands of pages of previously unreleased COVID-related documents public so Americans could read them for themselves.

Next year I will bring that same approach to the Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions (HELP) Committee as Ranking Member. As a physician and the author of dozens of bills on health care, education, and labor, I know the issues before this committee affect nearly every American family, from the cost of health care and how schools serve our children to how people earn a living and save for retirement.

Too many in Washington answer these questions with more government, and the coming Congress will bring a rush toward socialism unlike anything we have seen. Families, not federal bureaucrats, should make the decisions that shape their lives. I will stand against efforts to put Washington between Americans and their doctors, their children's schools, and their paychecks.
